# 0016: Agent discovery documents are generated by the Worker

Status: Accepted. Date: 2026-10-20.

## Context

Agents and crawlers look for `robots.txt`, `llms.txt`, an MCP server card and
an RFC 9727 API catalog before they connect. Assets use single-page-application
fallback, so every one of those paths returned the app's HTML with a 200,
which a client reads as a real (and unparseable) file. Static files in
`public/` would fix the status but not the content: the origin differs
between production and staging, and the tool list, protocol versions and
OAuth URLs already live in code.

## Decision

- The Worker serves `/robots.txt`, `/llms.txt`,
  `/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json` and `/.well-known/api-catalog` from
  `src/server/routes/discovery.ts`. `/robots.txt` and `/llms.txt` are listed in
  `run_worker_first`; `/.well-known/*` already was.
- Each is built from the constants the MCP and OAuth routes use (tool
  descriptors, server info, instructions, protocol versions, metadata URLs)
  and from the request origin, so it cannot drift from what the endpoint does.
- The server card and catalog 404 when agent access is off, like the OAuth
  metadata. `llms.txt` stays, saying agent access is not enabled.
- Only production `robots.txt` admits crawlers, to the front page,
  `llms.txt` and `/.well-known/` only. Public column links are unlisted and
  stay out of indexes. Content Signals: `search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=no`.
- Nothing served here describes anyone's data, and nothing needs a login.

## Consequences

- Other unknown paths still get the SPA shell with a 200; only these names
  are claimed.
- Not adopted: Markdown content negotiation and a sitemap (there is no public
  content), Web Bot Auth (nothing to sign), commerce protocols (nothing to sell).
  The server card follows the draft MCP server card shape and may need to
  change when that is finalized.
